title: The Due cell shows the earliest candidate; Other triggers lists the rest
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as a service advisor with the view customers and create and edit customers permissions.
  2. Seed asset A (e.g. unit 402)'s reading history by hand (standard steps; Mark complete on a work order records that work order's mileage and engine hours as readings dated its Reset date):
  3. ↳ In Settings > Maintenance (needs Settings Service) create, once, a throwaway schedule "ZZAUTOTEST Reading seed" with one routine service per reading: "ZZ Seed 1", "ZZ Seed 2", "ZZ Seed 3" (calendar Every 12 months each). Enrol the unit on it (its Maintenance tab > Enroll in Schedule, dates blank).
  4. ↳ For each reading below, oldest first: Work Orders > New Work Order for the unit; type the mileage (and the engine hours, where given) in the work order's Mileage (and Engine Hours) field; on that work order's maintenance card open the next "ZZ Seed" service's row menu > Mark complete > On a work order (this work order) > Reset date = the date given > Mark complete. A Reset date is never in the future.
  5. ↳ Readings: ZZ Seed 1: Reset date 90 days before today, Mileage 100,000, Engine Hours 5,000; ZZ Seed 2: Reset date 60 days before today, Mileage 103,000, Engine Hours 5,150; ZZ Seed 3: Reset date 30 days before today, Mileage 106,000, Engine Hours 5,300.
  6. ↳ Then remove the unit from the throwaway schedule (Maintenance tab > schedule menu > Remove from schedule), and enrol it on a schedule with PM-C (calendar Every 12 months + Distance Every 60,000 mileage + Engine hours Every 1,000 hours), dates blank. A unit whose past invoiced work orders already carry the same history may be used instead.
  7. Asset B: a new test unit created with Mileage left empty (Customers > the customer > Assets > New Asset), enrolled with blank dates on a schedule with "TIRES" (calendar Every 6 months + Distance Every 90,000 mileage).
custom_steps:
1. On asset A read PM-C's Due cell: how many dates and which trigger.
  2. Open PM-C's row menu > Other triggers and read the list.
  3. On asset B read the TIRES row.
  4. Hover the (i) on the Due column heading.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The Due cell shows one line: the earliest date and the trigger that produced it.
  • Other triggers lists every candidate date with its trigger, the earliest one marked "First".
  • TIRES shows its calendar date and reads "Calendar · needs mileage reading"; this is styled as an ordinary row, not a warning.
  • On the design the (i) reads "The earliest candidate and the trigger that produced it. Other candidates are in the row menu. A date known only to the month shows the month. Every estimate shows a month with its confidence; once due, the badge carries it."

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10566 (S9, The asset Maintenance tab), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S9 (The list beneath them; S9-R12, S9-N3); Plan 1 — Track, act, clear — Technical Implementation Plan, section 6 Phase P5, frontend table (OtherTriggersMenu); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard P4 and artboard S4; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.
